derivation:
simpa [Scheme.Modules.Hom.app, Scheme.Modules.presheaf, PresheafOfModules.presheaf_map_apply_coe] using
  (PresheafOfModules.naturality_apply (C := X.Opens) φ.val (homOfLE hle).op x).symm
explanation: Mathlib states (Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Presheaf.lean, line 125) `PresheafOfModules.naturality_apply (f : M₁ ⟶ M₂) (g : X ⟶ Y) (x : M₁.obj X) : Hom.app f Y (M₁.map g x) = M₂.map g (Hom.app f X x)`, i.e. naturality of `app` for morphisms of presheaves of modules. The judged theorem is exactly this statement for the presheaf-of-modules underlying a morphism `φ : P ⟶ Q` of `X.Modules` (with `M₁ := P.val`, `M₂ := Q.val`, `f := φ.val`, `X := op V`, `Y := op V'`, `g := (homOfLE hle).op`, sides swapped). The only differences are notational: in `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules` (`AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean`) `P.presheaf` is definitionally `P.val.presheaf` (so `presheaf.map _ x` is `val.map _ x`, `PresheafOfModules.presheaf_map_apply_coe`), and `Hom.app φ U` is `(forget₂ _ _).map (φ.val.app (op U))`, which is `AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (φ.val.app (op U)).hom` by the rfl-lemma `ModuleCat.forget₂_map`. Hence the result follows from that single Mathlib lemma by instantiating it to the sheaf-of-modules data plus routine unfolding/simp; the library's own proof instead goes through `φ.mapPresheaf.naturality` and `congrArg`, so it does not use this declaration.
